features.name: Regional files in the web app

tests.name: The catalog rejects a test entry that breaks the classification rules, and feature filters return each matching test once.
tests.methodology: Builds a sample catalog in memory, breaks one classification rule at a time, and checks that validation names that break, including a malformed catalog test identifier and a category prefix that does not match its category. It also checks that a feature filter returns each matching sample once. With synthetic Playwright JSON, it checks that the stored result is the final attempt: a later pass after an earlier failure or inconclusive attempt is passed with a passed-after-retry record, a single pass has no flag, a final failure stays failed, and a final inconclusive attempt stays inconclusive. It does not open the catalog page, require the live catalog to contain zero tests, or run an application test. It checks that a Bug Check requires a nonempty bug reference and root cause analysis on a Feature Behavior Test, and that a baseline test leaves both null.

tests.name: The release check runs the core tests first and stops before feature tests if a core test fails.
tests.methodology: Calls the same release-gate function the release command uses, with stand-in results. It checks that core runs first and that a failing or inconclusive core result stops the feature phase. It does not run the application or a real failing core test.

tests.name: Direct bucket address is refused, while a signed-in user's temporary link downloads the national layer file.
tests.methodology: Proves that a national layer file cannot be opened from its plain bucket address, while a signed-in active user can download it through the temporary link the service returns. File requested: inputs/reference/ramsar/v0.1.0/ramsar.geojson (Ramsar wetlands geometry, listed as national in the download catalog), once through the service and once at its plain storage.googleapis.com address; the DMT_TEST_NATIONAL_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Signs in a throwaway active account (role user, no SIRAP grant) and calls POST /downloads/signed-url on the deployed Metrics API for that file. It checks a 200 reply with a url, an expires_at between 14 and 16 minutes from now, and Cache-Control: no-store. It then makes a ranged GET for the first 1024 bytes on the returned link and expects 200 or 206 with bytes, and makes an anonymous GET of the same file's plain storage.googleapis.com address and expects 401 or 403. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked, and Firebase issues the ID token after a real email-and-password sign-in. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, and the chosen national object key; the user and record are deleted afterward. Not checked: the web app's download button, server cache timing, 503 configuration errors, or that the link stops working after its 15-minute expiry; 'temporary' is checked only through the reported expires_at time.

tests.name: A visitor who is not signed in cannot download a restricted regional file.
tests.methodology: Proves that a visitor with no sign-in gets no download link for a regional (SIRAP) file and cannot open it from its plain bucket address either. File requested: inputs/reference/orinoquia_savannas/v0.1.0/orinoquia_savannas.metadata.json (Orinoquia savannas metadata, listed as restricted to the orinoquia region), twice through the service and once at its plain storage.googleapis.com address; the DMT_TEST_ORINOQUIA_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Calls POST /downloads/signed-url on the deployed Metrics API for that file with no Authorization header, then with a made-up bearer string that is not a Firebase ID token, and expects 401 with reason invalid_token each time. No reply body may contain a url, and no raw reply text may contain X-Goog-Signature. It then makes an anonymous GET of the file's plain storage.googleapis.com address and expects 401 or 403. Real: the deployed Metrics API, including its Firebase ID token check, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the made-up token string and the chosen Orinoquia object key; no Firebase account is created. Not checked: expired, revoked, or other-project tokens, signed-in accounts (FBT-003 and FBT-007 cover those), the Eje Cafetero file, the web app's download button, server cache timing, or 503 configuration errors.

tests.name: A signed-in user with no regional (SIRAP) access cannot download a restricted regional file.
tests.methodology: Proves that a signed-in active user who passed the authenticator sign-in but holds no regional (SIRAP) grant gets no download link for a regional file and cannot open it from its plain bucket address either. File requested: inputs/reference/orinoquia_savannas/v0.1.0/orinoquia_savannas.metadata.json (Orinoquia savannas metadata, listed as restricted to the orinoquia region), once through the service and once at its plain storage.googleapis.com address; the DMT_TEST_ORINOQUIA_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Creates an active account with role user and an empty allowedSirapIds list, enrolls a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator, then signs in again with password plus code, so Firebase marks its ID token's second factor as totp. Asking POST /downloads/signed-url for the file, it expects 403 with reason layer_forbidden; the reply body may not contain a url and the raw reply text may not contain X-Goog-Signature. It then makes an anonymous GET of the file's plain storage.googleapis.com address and expects 401 or 403. Because the authenticator sign-in is present, the refusal isolates the region-grant rule; FBT-003 covers the refusal without an authenticator (mfa_required). Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, authenticator codes computed in memory from the enrollment secret, and the chosen Orinoquia object key; the user and record are deleted afterward. Not checked: a sirap-user granted a different region (FBT-003 covers that with the Eje Cafetero file), the Eje Cafetero file itself, how fast a revoked grant takes effect, the web app's download button, server cache timing, or 503 configuration errors.

tests.name: Download links are refused when the sign-in is missing, fake, or from a pending account.
tests.methodology: Proves that the service gives no download link when the request has no sign-in, a fake sign-in, or a real sign-in from an account still pending approval. File requested: inputs/reference/ramsar/v0.1.0/ramsar.geojson (Ramsar wetlands geometry, listed as national in the download catalog), three times through the service; the DMT_TEST_NATIONAL_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Calls POST /downloads/signed-url on the deployed Metrics API for that file with no Authorization header, with a made-up bearer string that is not a Firebase ID token, and with a real ID token for an account whose Firestore status is pending (role user, no authenticator). It expects 401, 401, and 403 with reason account_inactive, and checks that no reply body has a url and no raw reply text contains X-Goog-Signature. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked, and Firebase issues the pending account's ID token after a real email-and-password sign-in. Test-only: the pending Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, the made-up token string, and the chosen national object key; the user and record are deleted afterward. Not checked: expired, revoked, or other-project tokens, the 401 refusal reason, the web app's download button, server cache timing, 503 configuration errors, or the 15-minute link expiry.

tests.name: A regional (SIRAP) layer download is refused without authenticator sign-in or without that region's grant.
tests.methodology: Proves that a regional (SIRAP) file is refused to an account that signed in without an authenticator and to an authenticator account that lacks that region's grant, while an authenticator account holding the grant can download it. Files requested: inputs/reference/orinoquia_savannas/v0.1.0/orinoquia_savannas.metadata.json (Orinoquia savannas metadata, listed as restricted to the orinoquia region), then inputs/reference/eje_cafetero_wetlands/v0.1.0/eje_cafetero_wetlands.metadata.json (Eje Cafetero wetlands metadata, listed as restricted to the eje-cafetero region); the DMT_TEST_ORINOQUIA_OBJECT and DMT_TEST_EJE_CAFETERO_OBJECT environment variables can override the keys. Creates two active accounts with role sirap-user and allowedSirapIds ['orinoquia']. The first signs in with a password only. The second enrolls a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator, then signs in again with password plus code, so Firebase marks its ID token's second factor as totp. Asking POST /downloads/signed-url for the Orinoquia file, the password-only account gets 403 mfa_required with no link, and the authenticator account gets 200 with a link whose ranged GET returns 200 or 206 with bytes. The authenticator account asking for the Eje Cafetero file gets 403 layer_forbidden with no link. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the two Firebase users, created by the Admin SDK with verified @dmt-test.invalid addresses so no email is sent, their Firestore users records, authenticator codes computed in memory from the enrollment secret, and the chosen Orinoquia and Eje Cafetero object keys; users and records are deleted afterward. Not checked: SMS second factors, the sirap-admin role, how fast a revoked grant takes effect, the plain bucket address, the web app's download button, server cache timing, 503 configuration errors, or the 15-minute link expiry.

tests.name: A super-admin with authenticator sign-in can download both regional (SIRAP) layers without region grants.
tests.methodology: Proves that a super-admin who signed in with an authenticator can download the files of both regions (SIRAP) even with an empty region-grant list. Files requested: inputs/reference/orinoquia_savannas/v0.1.0/orinoquia_savannas.metadata.json (Orinoquia savannas metadata, listed as restricted to the orinoquia region) and inputs/reference/eje_cafetero_wetlands/v0.1.0/eje_cafetero_wetlands.metadata.json (Eje Cafetero wetlands metadata, listed as restricted to the eje-cafetero region); the DMT_TEST_ORINOQUIA_OBJECT and DMT_TEST_EJE_CAFETERO_OBJECT environment variables can override the keys. Creates an active account with Firestore role super-admin and an empty allowedSirapIds list, enrolls a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator, and signs in again with password plus code. It asks POST /downloads/signed-url for the Orinoquia file and the Eje Cafetero file, expects 200 with a link for each, and expects a ranged GET on each link to return 200 or 206 with bytes. Because the grant list is empty, both regions must come from the super-admin role. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, authenticator codes computed in memory, and the chosen Orinoquia and Eje Cafetero object keys; the user and record are deleted afterward. Not checked: a super-admin without an authenticator, national files, the web app's download button, server cache timing, 503 configuration errors, or the 15-minute link expiry.

tests.name: A file in the bucket but missing from the download catalog is refused, including ../ path tricks.
tests.methodology: Proves that the service refuses a file that exists in the bucket but is missing from the download catalog, and refuses a key starting with '../' even when the rest of it names a listed file. Files requested: releases/catalog-v3-7-1/manifest.json (a real 74 MB bucket object that the download catalog deliberately leaves out), then the path-shaped key ../inputs/reference/ramsar/v0.1.0/ramsar.geojson ('../' followed by the Ramsar wetlands geometry key, which is listed as national); the DMT_TEST_UNLISTED_OBJECT and DMT_TEST_NATIONAL_OBJECT environment variables can override the keys. With a real ID token for an active account (role user, no SIRAP grant), asks POST /downloads/signed-url for the unlisted key and expects 404 object_not_in_catalog with no link. It then asks for the path-shaped key and expects 422 with no link, so a path-shaped key is refused even when it points at a listed file. No reply body may contain a url, and no raw reply text may contain X-Goog-Signature. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication, Firestore, and the deployed download catalog; nothing in the request path is mocked, and Firebase issues the ID token after a real email-and-password sign-in. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, and the chosen unlisted and national object keys; the user and record are deleted afterward. The test does not itself verify that the unlisted key exists in the bucket; that is a precondition of the chosen key. Not checked: other malformed keys such as URLs or backslashes, the web app's download button, server cache timing, or 503 configuration errors.

tests.name: A signed-in user with authenticator sign-in and a region grant can download that region's restricted file.
tests.methodology: Proves that a signed-in active user who passed the authenticator sign-in and holds a regional (SIRAP) grant gets a working temporary download link for that region's restricted file. File requested: inputs/reference/eje_cafetero_wetlands/v0.1.0/eje_cafetero_wetlands.metadata.json (Eje Cafetero wetlands metadata, listed as restricted to the eje-cafetero region); the DMT_TEST_EJE_CAFETERO_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Creates an active account with role sirap-user and allowedSirapIds ['eje-cafetero'], enrolls a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator, then signs in again with password plus code, so Firebase marks its ID token's second factor as totp. Calls POST /downloads/signed-url on the deployed Metrics API for the file and expects a 200 reply with a url, an expires_at between 14 and 16 minutes from now, and Cache-Control: no-store. It then makes a ranged GET for the first 1024 bytes on the returned link and expects 200 or 206 with bytes. Because the account has a grant and no super-admin role, the success comes from the region grant itself, and it covers the second region that FBT-003 does not download. Real: the deployed Metrics API, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in, Firestore, and the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, authenticator codes computed in memory from the enrollment secret, and the chosen Eje Cafetero object key; the user and record are deleted afterward. Not checked: an Eje Cafetero-granted account asking for the Orinoquia file (FBT-003 covers the reverse), the password-only sign-in refusal (FBT-003), the no-grant refusal (FBT-007), super-admin access (FBT-004), how fast a revoked grant takes effect, the plain bucket address, the web app's download button, server cache timing, or 503 configuration errors.

tests.name: Every file the app shows only to regional users can be opened only through a signed link.
tests.methodology: Proves that every file the web app shows only to regional (SIRAP) users, meaning map layers, metadata, metrics, and solutions, opens only through a temporary signed link from the signing service, never from its plain bucket address or its old public Vercel Blob address. Files requested: every regional-only file in the published manifests. The test reads the catalog release index the production web app loads (catalog-releases/3.7.1/catalog-release-index.json today, from frontend/shared/runtime-manifest.constants.mjs; DMT_TEST_CATALOG_RELEASE_INDEX_URL can override it) and every manifest it lists. A layer or solution with a nonempty sirapId is regional; every string in it that names a stored file (a public Vercel Blob or storage.googleapis.com address, a gs:// address, or a relative *Path value) is a reference. A file is regional-only when only records of one region reference it. Left out and listed in the attached findings: files a national record also references, files reached only through the Colombia-wide fields mecNationalDenominator, speciesGoalsCatalog, and speciesGoalsTargetOverlay, and files used by more than one region. What it checks: for each regional-only file, an anonymous HEAD of its old public Vercel Blob address returns 404 or 403; an anonymous HEAD of its plain storage.googleapis.com address returns 401 or 403; POST /downloads/signed-url on the deployed Metrics API refuses an active authenticator-signed-in account with no region grant (403 or 404, no url, no X-Goog-Signature); and the download catalog tags the file with its own region. The service does not expose its catalog, so the tag is read from its decisions: the no-grant account must get 403 layer_forbidden (tagged regional, not national, not missing), and an account granted only the file's region must get a link (tagged with that region, not the other one). For each region, the first file by key whose granted link was issued is downloaded with a ranged GET of 1024 bytes and must return 200 or 206 with bytes. Checks run with at most 16 requests in flight per host (DMT_TEST_BULK_CHECK_CONCURRENCY), every result is collected before asserting, and each check reports its failure count, counts by status, and the first five object keys; an attached JSON lists every failing key with statuses and never a signed link. A 429, a 5xx, or no reply is inconclusive with its reason; the test reports INCONCLUSIVE only when nothing failed outright. Real: the published manifests, Vercel Blob, the Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket, the deployed Metrics API and its download catalog, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and second-factor sign-in, and Firestore; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: one active account with role user and no grant, and one sirap-user account per region granted only that region, each created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, each with an authenticator enrolled and codes computed in memory; accounts and records are deleted afterward. Not checked: files inside nested manifests such as the species manifest, whether every regional file exists in the bucket (only one sample per region is downloaded), the web app's own requests or download button, super-admin access, password-only sign-in, server cache timing, or the 15-minute link expiry.

tests.name: A signed-in user cannot give themselves regional access, a higher role, or reactivate a denied account by editing their own record.
tests.methodology: Proves that the deployed Firestore security rules refuse every edit a person makes to their own users record, so the signing service, which trusts that record, keeps refusing them. File requested: inputs/reference/orinoquia_savannas/v0.1.0/orinoquia_savannas.metadata.json (Orinoquia savannas metadata, listed as restricted to the orinoquia region), twice through the service; the DMT_TEST_ORINOQUIA_OBJECT environment variable can override the key. Creates an active account (role user, empty allowedSirapIds) and a denied account (role user), each with an enrolled Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator and signed in again with password plus code. Through the Firebase client library signed in as each account, the active account tries to update its own users record to add orinoquia to allowedSirapIds (as role sirap-user), to set role super-admin, and to set role sirap-admin administering orinoquia; the denied account tries to set its own status to active. Every payload is shaped like the web app's real admin writes (tier, updatedAt server time, updatedBy), so only the self-edit makes it wrong. Each write must fail with permission-denied. An Admin SDK read then shows both records identical to the copies read right after creation. Asking POST /downloads/signed-url for the file, the active account gets 403 layer_forbidden and the denied account gets 403 account_inactive, with no url in either body and no X-Goog-Signature in either raw reply. Real: the deployed Firestore security rules, Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in, and the deployed Metrics API; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the two Firebase users, created by the Admin SDK with verified @dmt-test.invalid addresses so no email is sent, their Firestore users records, authenticator codes computed in memory, and the chosen Orinoquia object key; users and records are deleted afterward. Not checked: the repository copy of firestore.rules (only the deployed rules are exercised), edits by admins (FBT-027 covers regional admins), self-created records for accounts with no record yet, pending accounts, the web app's screens, or server cache timing.

tests.name: A regional admin can grant only the regions they administer.
tests.methodology: Proves that the deployed Firestore security rules let a regional (SIRAP) admin grant their own region, and refuse a grant for a region they do not administer or on a super-admin's record. Creates an active Orinoquia regional admin (role sirap-admin, allowedSirapIds and administeredSirapIds ['orinoquia']) with an enrolled Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator and a second sign-in with password plus code, an active ordinary account (role user, no region), and an active super-admin account. Through the Firebase client library signed in as the regional admin, it sends the same update the web app's regional grant sends (allowedSirapIds, role sirap-user, tier 2, updatedAt server time, updatedBy the admin). Granting ['orinoquia'] to the ordinary account must succeed, and an Admin SDK read must show allowedSirapIds ['orinoquia'] and role sirap-user. Granting ['orinoquia', 'eje-cafetero'] to the same account must fail with permission-denied, and the record must still hold only orinoquia. Sending the same Orinoquia grant to the super-admin's record must fail with permission-denied, and an Admin SDK read must show that record identical to the copy read right after creation. Real: the deployed Firestore security rules and Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the three Firebase users, created by the Admin SDK with verified @dmt-test.invalid addresses so no email is sent, and their Firestore users records; users and records are deleted afterward. Not checked: the repository copy of firestore.rules, revoking a region, an Eje Cafetero admin, editing another regional admin, approving access requests, the signing service's reaction to the grant (FBT-003 and FBT-008 cover granted downloads), or the web app's screens.

tests.name: A person cannot approve their own regional access request.
tests.methodology: Proves that the deployed Firestore security rules let a person file their own pending regional (SIRAP) access request but refuse when that person marks it approved. Creates an active account (role user, empty allowedSirapIds) with an enrolled Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authenticator and a second sign-in with password plus code. Through the Firebase client library signed in as that account, it creates sirapAccessRequests/{uid}_orinoquia with the fields the web app sends (uid, email, displayName, sirapId orinoquia, status pending, reason null, requestedAt and updatedAt server time); the write must succeed and an Admin SDK read must show status pending. It then updates the request to status approved with decidedAt, decidedBy itself, and updatedAt; the write must fail with permission-denied, and an Admin SDK read must still show status pending with no decidedBy. A final Admin SDK read shows the account's users record still has role user and an empty allowedSirapIds. Real: the deployed Firestore security rules and Firebase Authentication including authenticator enrollment and the second-factor sign-in; nothing in the request path is mocked. Test-only: the Firebase user, created by the Admin SDK with a verified @dmt-test.invalid address so no email is sent, its Firestore users record, and its access request; all are deleted afterward. Not checked: the repository copy of firestore.rules, a regional admin or super-admin approving their own request, re-requesting after a denial, a request filed without an authenticator, Eje Cafetero requests, or the web app's screens.
